Love,
Swati

"Rafiq, just paste your whole report card in. It'll tell you which subject to focus on."
"With my name and roll number on top? No."
"Why not? It's just a computer."
"Do you know where it keeps what I type, Naveen?"
"...No."
"Me neither. That's the problem."
"But it'll give better advice with real details."
"I can give it just the numbers. 'Maths 58, science 72, English 81, which should I focus on?' No name, no school, no address."
"And the group project? You were going to paste everyone's parts in."
"I'll paste only mine. Aarav and Sneha didn't say yes to their writing going in."
"You're so paranoid."
"Maybe. But once it's typed, I can't un-type it."

qa.q: What does Rafiq refuse to paste?
qa.a: The report card with name and roll number on top.

qa.q: Why is Rafiq cautious about the AI?
qa.a: Rafiq feels wary because nobody knows where the typed information is kept, and it can't be un-typed later.

qa.q: What else could Rafiq do before using a new AI tool?
qa.a: Rafiq could read the tool's privacy notes or ask a teacher which tools the school trusts.

qa.q: How might Aarav and Sneha feel about Rafiq's choice?
qa.a: They would likely be glad their writing wasn't shared without being asked.

grounding: Shows a student choosing not to enter a name, marks or friends' work into an AI tool because nobody knows how it is stored or used.

subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: protecting privacy when using AI [Thinking]
passage: When I was filling in a scholarship form in Class 12, I nearly pasted my whole life into an AI tool. I'm Irfan. The form wanted a personal statement, and I thought the tool could help more if it knew everything: my full name, our address in Aligarh, my board marks, even the story of my friend Madhuri getting me through maths. My cursor was on send when I stopped. Where does this go? Who reads it? I honestly didn't know. And Madhuri's story wasn't mine to share without asking. So I deleted the details and asked a general question instead: "What makes a personal statement clear and honest?" I wrote the actual statement myself, in a notebook. Looking back, it took longer, but nothing about me or my friend is sitting on some server I've never seen.

qa.q: What general question did Irfan ask instead?
qa.a: What makes a personal statement clear and honest?

qa.q: What was Irfan feeling with the cursor on send?
qa.a: Irfan felt a sudden unease, unsure where the information would go or who would read it.

qa.q: What else could Irfan have done to get help with the statement?
qa.a: Irfan could ask a teacher or counsellor to read the draft, since they can give feedback without the details going to an unknown tool.

qa.q: How might Madhuri feel about Irfan's choice?
qa.a: Madhuri would likely feel respected that the maths story wasn't shared without being asked.

grounding: Illustrates a student deciding not to type a full name, address, marks or a friend's story into an AI tool, since how it is stored is unknown.
